incident: From IcedID to Dagon Locker ransomware in 29 days (DFIR Report, intrusion Aug 2023, published 2024-04-29)

sources.title: From IcedID to Dagon Locker Ransomware in 29 Days - The DFIR Report (2024-04-29)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (PrometheusTDS phishing JS -> IcedID on beachhead), hops (Cobalt Strike SMB beacon to DC via remote service, WMIC beacons to more hosts, GPO logon-script distribution), exfil (Rclone + AWSCollector to AWS S3), TTR 684h / 29 days, Dagon Locker domain-wide

narrative_before: In August 2023 a PrometheusTDS phishing chain led a victim to a fake Azure portal and a malicious JavaScript file that used curl to download and run an IcedID DLL on a beachhead host, with scheduled-task persistence (DFIR Report). After ~30 hours IcedID fetched a Cobalt Strike beacon (staged on file.io). The actor ran net/whoami/nltest discovery, accessed LSASS, used GetSystem for privilege escalation, and within five minutes moved a Cobalt Strike beacon over SMB to a domain controller, executing it via remote services. Using AdFind/Sharefinder they mapped shares, briefly used Rclone, then switched to a custom AWSCollector PowerShell tool to exfiltrate data to an AWS S3 bucket; more beacons were pushed to additional hosts by SMB copy + WMIC. On day 8 they installed AnyDesk on a domain controller (plus a new admin account) and worked through Group Policy, later creating a logon script to distribute beacons to a privileged user group. After repeated return visits over the following weeks, on day 29 they staged Dagon Locker on a domain controller and used AWSCollector's locker module to deploy it via SMB to remote hosts, with a batch script to disable services and delete shadow copies - domain-wide encryption. Time to ransomware was 684 hours over 29 days (DFIR Report).

detection_moments.description: Initial compromise: PrometheusTDS phishing JS downloads and runs IcedID DLL on the beachhead with scheduled-task persistence; ~30 hours later Cobalt Strike is fetched.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Upon executing this file... a batch file used the curl command to download an IcedID DLL file... IcedID malware established persistence by creating a scheduled task... About 30 hours after inactivity, the IcedID malware downloaded and executed a Cobalt Strike beacon.' - DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: Day 1-2 hands-on expansion: LSASS + GetSystem on beachhead, Cobalt Strike beacon to the DC via remote service within 5 minutes, AdFind/Sharefinder on shares, Rclone/AWSCollector exfil to S3, beacons pushed to more hosts via WMIC.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Within just five minutes of executing the Cobalt Strike beacon, the threat actor initiated lateral movement... They transferred a Cobalt Strike beacon to a domain controller using SMB... executed via remote services.' - DFIR Report

attack_path: Cobalt Strike beacon copied over SMB to DC and executed via remote service; later AnyDesk + GPO logon-script abuse - T1021.002 / T1569.002 / T1484.001
share discovery (AdFind/Sharefinder), Rclone then AWSCollector exfil to AWS S3 - T1083 / T1567.002
Cobalt Strike beacon copied via SMB/copy and executed by remote WMIC - T1021.002 / T1047
Dagon Locker staged on DC, deployed via SMB by AWSCollector locker module; batch disables services and deletes shadow copies - T1021.002 / T1486 / T1490
ambiguities: Report does not state victim detection; m1 = initial IcedID execution, m2 = first active lateral-movement day (DC compromise + exfil start).
Counts of 'additional hosts' receiving beacons and of domain-wide encrypted hosts not quantified; represented as srv_1 and pc_1..pc_3 (generic).
Number of domain controllers not quantified; modelled as one.
workstation->dc/files links not added for generic encrypted hosts pc_1..pc_3 because their individual credential use is not described; they receive the locker from the DC.
